stated: Reform UK will commence recruitment to increase UK per capita police numbers to 300 per 100,000 population, adding 40,000 new front-line officers over a five-year parliament.

source.quote: Commence Increase in Police Numbers Recruitment to increase UK per capita police numbers to 300 per 100k population. That is 40,000 new front-line officers, over a 5-year parliament.

bearing_set.reason: Adding 40,000 front-line officers directly affects policing capacity, crime deterrence, and public safety — a non-negligible effect on safety and security.

40,000 officers at an estimated all-in cost of ~£55–70k per officer per year implies a recurring additional spend of roughly £2.2–2.8bn annually; absent a named funding source this materially affects the funded-vs-borrowed balance and debt-path sustainability, the central O12 indicators.

membership_note: O10 is not included: the policy adds personnel, not new coercive powers — existing powers exercised more widely do not meet the O10 threshold of 'adds coercive/surveillance power'. O11 is not included: no specific tax measure is attached, so the fiscal strain routes to O12. O13 and O15 effects are too indirect and speculative to clear the non-negligible bar.
